learn.hook: x is just a number wearing a disguise. Polynomials are what you build when you play with such letter-numbers!
points: An algebraic expression is made of terms. In 4x² − 3x + 7, the terms are 4x², −3x and 7; x is the variable (a letter-number), 4 and −3 are coefficients, and 7 is the constant.
A polynomial in one variable (univariate) uses only one letter, with whole-number powers 0, 1, 2, 3, ...
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of its variable that appears with a non-zero coefficient.
By degree: constant (0), linear (1), quadratic (2), cubic (3).
A constant like 8 can be written 8x⁰ (since x⁰ = 1), so its degree is 0.

example.q: Find the degree and the type of p(x) = 5 − 2x + x³ − 4x².

learn.reallife: A shopkeeper's bill rule like 'price × quantity + delivery charge' is a polynomial in the quantity.

quiz.q: What is the degree of 3x⁴ − 7x² + x − 10?
quiz.explain: The highest power of x is 4.
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of terms instead of the highest power

quiz.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 12?
quiz.explain: 12 = 12x⁰, so the highest power of x is 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a constant has degree 1 or equal to its value

quiz.q: Which is a quadratic polynomial?
quiz.explain: A quadratic has degree 2. In 5 − x² the highest power is 2.
quiz.mistake: Calls any polynomial with a square in it quadratic even when a cube is present

quiz.q: How many terms are there in 8y³ − y + 2?
quiz.explain: The terms are 8y³, −y and 2.
quiz.mistake: Counts the coefficient 8 as the number of terms

quiz.q: Which expression is NOT a polynomial in one variable?
quiz.explain: x² + y has two different variables, x and y.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a constant cannot be a polynomial

quiz.q: Why is the degree of 9 equal to 0?
quiz.explain: Any non-zero constant can be written with x⁰, so the highest power is 0.
quiz.mistake: Confuses degree with the size of the number

quiz.q: In 2x − 7x³ + 4, which term decides the degree?
quiz.explain: −7x³ has the highest power, 3, so the polynomial is cubic.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first term written as the leading term

quiz.q: Which is a cubic polynomial?
quiz.explain: x − x³ has highest power 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the order of terms decides the degree

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What is the degree of a polynomial, and what is a quadratic?"
teach.praise: Yes! The highest power decides the degree, and 2 means quadratic!
teach.nudge: Which power do you look at to find the degree? What degree is a quadratic?

learn.hook: A polynomial is a machine: drop in a number, turn the handle, and out pops its value!
points: The coefficient of a power is the number multiplying it. In 3x² − x + 5, the coefficient of x is −1.
If a power is missing, its coefficient is 0. In x³ + 2, the coefficient of x² is 0.
The constant term is the term with no variable (the coefficient of x⁰).
To evaluate p(x) at x = k, replace every x by k, using brackets for negatives: p(−2) for x² gives (−2)² = 4.
You can write a polynomial of any degree you like: 2x² − 1 is one example of degree 2.
learn.reallife: An electricity bill formula with a fixed meter charge plus a rate per unit is evaluated each month at a new number of units.

items.text: In 4x³ − x + 6, the coefficient of x is ___.
In 4x³ − x + 6, the coefficient of x² is ___.
In 4x³ − x + 6, the constant term is ___.

quiz.q: What is the coefficient of x² in 7x³ − 4x + 9?
quiz.explain: There is no x² term, so its coefficient is 0.
quiz.mistake: Picks a coefficient of some other power when a term is missing

quiz.q: What is the coefficient of x in 5 − x + 2x²?
quiz.explain: The term −x means −1 × x.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the minus sign or thinks a hidden 1 is 0

quiz.q: What is the constant term of 3x² − 8x − 11?
quiz.explain: The term without x is −11; the sign belongs to it.
quiz.mistake: Drops the sign of the constant term

quiz.q: If p(x) = x² − 4x + 3, find p(−1).
quiz.mistake: Writes (−1)² as −1

quiz.q: If q(x) = 3x² − 2, find q(−3).
quiz.explain: Square first: (−3)² = 9, then 3 × 9 − 2.
quiz.mistake: Squares −3 to get −9

quiz.q: A ball's height after t seconds is h(t) = 20t − 5t² metres. What is its height at t = 2?
quiz.mistake: Squares the 5t together or forgets to square t

quiz.q: Which is a polynomial of degree 3 with constant term −2?
quiz.explain: Its highest power is 3 and its constant is −2.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the coefficient 3 with the degree 3

quiz.q: If p(x) = 2x + 7, find p(−4) + p(4).
quiz.explain: p(−4) = −1 and p(4) = 15, so the sum is 14.
quiz.mistake: Thinks p(−4) and p(4) cancel to 0

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What is the coefficient of x² in x³ + 5, and how do I find p(−2)?"
teach.praise: Great! Missing term means coefficient 0, and you substitute carefully with brackets!
teach.nudge: What is the coefficient of a power that is missing? How do you put −2 into the polynomial?

learn.hook: An auto fare of ₹30 plus ₹15 for every km grows by the same amount each km. That steady growth is a linear polynomial!
points: A linear polynomial in x has the form ax + b, where a and b are numbers and a ≠ 0.
Its degree is 1: the highest power of x is x¹. Terms like x², 1/x or √x are not allowed.
a is the coefficient of x and b is the constant term.
To evaluate p(x) at x = k, replace x by k: p(k) = ak + b.
Each time x goes up by 1, the value of ax + b changes by exactly a.

example.q: A taxi charges ₹50 to start plus ₹12 per km. Write the fare for x km as a polynomial and find the fare for 8 km.

learn.reallife: Electricity bills, mobile data plans and taxi fares often have a fixed charge plus a charge per unit: a linear polynomial.

items.text: In 7x − 3, the coefficient of x is ___
The degree of a linear polynomial is ___

quiz.q: Which of these is a linear polynomial?
quiz.explain: 4x − 1 has the form ax + b with highest power of x equal to 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any expression with x is linear, even with x², x³ or x in the denominator

quiz.q: If p(x) = 3x − 7, find p(4).
quiz.explain: Replace x by 4 and simplify.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 instead of subtracting it, getting 19

quiz.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 6 − 2x?
quiz.explain: The highest power of x is x¹, so the degree is 1.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the degree with a coefficient or the constant term

quiz.q: Aisha's phone plan costs ₹99 fixed plus ₹2 per GB of data. Which polynomial gives the cost for x GB?
quiz.explain: The ₹2 is paid for each GB, so it multiplies x. The ₹99 is paid once, so it is the constant.
quiz.mistake: Attaches x to the fixed charge instead of the per-unit charge

quiz.q: For p(x) = 5x + 2, find p(−3).
quiz.mistake: Drops the negative sign when multiplying by −3

quiz.q: At a sports shop the price of x cricket balls is p(x) = 150x rupees. What is p(4) − p(3)?
quiz.explain: One extra ball adds the coefficient of x, ₹150, to the price.
quiz.mistake: Gives p(4) or p(3) instead of their difference

quiz.q: Which expression is NOT a linear polynomial?
quiz.explain: x(x + 1) = x² + x has degree 2, so it is not linear. x/3 + 1 is linear because x/3 = (1/3)x.
quiz.mistake: Thinks dividing x by a number makes it non-linear, or misses the hidden x²

quiz.q: If p(x) = ax + 4 and p(2) = 10, what is a?
quiz.explain: Put x = 2: 2a + 4 = 10, so 2a = 6 and a = 3.
quiz.mistake: Divides 10 by 2 without first subtracting 4

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What makes a polynomial 'linear'? It sounds like a line, but it is just letters and numbers!"
teach.praise: Highest power of x is one, like ax + b. And it really does make a line on a graph. Super!
teach.nudge: What is the highest power of x allowed in a linear polynomial?

learn.hook: A lemonade stall makes a loss at first and a profit later. The exact moment it breaks even is a zero of a polynomial!
points: A zero of p(x) is a value of x that makes p(x) = 0.
For p(x) = ax + b with a ≠ 0, solve ax + b = 0 to get the zero x = −b/a.
A linear polynomial has exactly one zero.
On the graph, the zero is where the line crosses the x-axis: the point (−b/a, 0).
To check a zero, substitute it: the answer must come out as 0.

example.q: Find the zero of p(x) = 3x − 12 and say where its graph meets the x-axis.
steps: The line meets the x-axis at (4, 0)
example.answer: x = 4; the graph crosses the x-axis at (4, 0)

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers find the break-even number of items, where profit is exactly zero, by finding the zero of a profit polynomial.

games.title: Match each polynomial with its zero

quiz.q: What is the zero of p(x) = x − 6?
quiz.explain: x − 6 = 0 gives x = 6. Check: 6 − 6 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Takes the constant with its sign (−6) as the zero

quiz.q: Find the zero of 4x + 20.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that moving +20 across makes it −20

quiz.q: Where does the graph of y = 2x − 10 cross the x-axis?
quiz.explain: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x − 10 = 0 and x = 5. The crossing point is (5, 0).
quiz.mistake: Gives the y-intercept (0, −10) instead of the x-axis crossing

quiz.q: How many zeros does a linear polynomial ax + b (with a ≠ 0) have?
quiz.explain: A non-horizontal straight line crosses the x-axis exactly once, at x = −b/a.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up linear polynomials with quadratics, which can have two zeros

quiz.q: Is x = 3 a zero of p(x) = 3x − 9?
quiz.explain: p(3) = 3 × 3 − 9 = 0, so 3 is a zero.
quiz.mistake: Substitutes x = 0 instead of x = 3

quiz.q: Arjun's lemonade stall makes a profit of p(x) = 5x − 150 rupees when he sells x glasses. How many glasses must he sell to break even (zero profit)?
quiz.explain: Break even means p(x) = 0: 5x = 150, so x = 30.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts or multiplies instead of dividing 150 by 5

quiz.q: The zero of 3x + k is 2. What is k?
quiz.explain: Since 2 is a zero, 3 × 2 + k = 0, so k = −6.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the sign and writes k = 6

quiz.q: What is the zero of p(x) = 2x + 3?
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round (−2/3) or loses the minus sign

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: "What is a 'zero' of a polynomial? Is it just the number 0?"
teach.praise: Oh! It is the x that makes the polynomial equal zero, where the line crosses the x-axis. Tweet-tastic!
teach.nudge: Is the zero a value of x or a value of p(x)? And where can I see it on the graph?

topics.title: Solving word problems with linear equations

learn.hook: Every puzzle that says 'think of a number' is secretly a linear equation waiting to be solved!
points: Set a linear polynomial equal to a value to get a linear equation, then solve for the unknown.
Steps: name the unknown, translate the words into an equation, solve, and check the answer in the story.
Ages: if Ravi is x now, in 5 years he is x + 5; numbers in a ratio 3 : 5 can be written 3k and 5k.
Coins: if there are x coins of ₹5, they are worth 5x rupees. Rectangle: perimeter = 2(l + b).
A two-digit number with tens digit x and units digit y is 10x + y; swapping the digits gives 10y + x, and the difference is 9(x − y).

example.q: A rectangular garden has perimeter 46 m and its length is 5 m more than its breadth. Find its dimensions.

learn.reallife: Splitting a restaurant bill or planning how many ₹10 and ₹20 notes make ₹500 are everyday linear-equation problems.

games.title: Digit tricks
items: The number with tens digit 4 and units digit 7 is 10 × 4 + 7.
A two-digit number minus its digit-swap is always a multiple of 9.
If two numbers are in ratio 2 : 3, they can be written 2k and 3k.
Any common multiplier k keeps the ratio 2 : 3.
x coins of ₹2 are worth x + 2 rupees.

quiz.q: Meera is 3 times as old as her brother. In 4 years their ages will add to 40. How old is her brother now?
quiz.explain: Let the brother be x; Meera is 3x. In 4 years: (x + 4) + (3x + 4) = 40.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 years to only one person

quiz.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7 and their sum is 88. What is the larger number?
quiz.explain: Write them as 4k and 7k. Then 11k = 88, so k = 8.
quiz.mistake: Finds k but forgets to multiply by 7

quiz.q: A piggy bank has ₹5 and ₹10 coins, 30 coins in all, worth ₹220. How many ₹10 coins are there?
quiz.explain: Let ₹10 coins be x; then ₹5 coins are 30 − x. 10x + 5(30 − x) = 220.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which coin count is x

quiz.q: A 50 m fence is cut into two pieces so that one is 8 m longer than the other. How long is the shorter piece?
quiz.mistake: Halves 50 without accounting for the difference

quiz.q: A rectangle's length is twice its breadth and its perimeter is 72 cm. What is its length?
quiz.explain: 2(2b + b) = 72, so 6b = 72 and b = 12. Length = 2b.
quiz.mistake: Gives the breadth instead of the length

quiz.q: The digits of a two-digit number add to 9. Swapping the digits makes the number 27 more. What is the number?
quiz.explain: Let digits be x (tens) and y (units). Swap minus original = 9(y − x) = 27, so y − x = 3; with x + y = 9, x = 3 and y = 6.
quiz.mistake: Writes the swapped number in place of the original

quiz.q: Which expression stands for a two-digit number with tens digit a and units digit b?
quiz.explain: The tens digit is worth 10 times its face value.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side as a product

quiz.q: Sunil thinks of a number, multiplies it by 5 and subtracts 12 to get 43. What was his number?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 12 instead of adding it back

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I turn a story problem into an equation?"
teach.praise: Wonderful! Name the unknown, form the equation, solve and check!
teach.nudge: What do you call the thing you don't know? And how do you make sure your answer fits the story?

learn.hook: Matchsticks, tiles, rickshaw fares: if each step adds the same amount, one short rule predicts them all!
points: In a linear pattern each stage adds the same amount. Tiles 1, 3, 5, 7, ... add 2 each time, so stage n has 2n − 1 tiles.
General rule: if stage 1 has f and each stage adds d, stage n has f + (n − 1)d.
Use the rule forwards (find stage 50) or backwards (which stage has 99 tiles?). If the stage number is not a whole number, that count is impossible.
Real life: an auto fare of ₹30 plus ₹15 per km, pocket money left after spending ₹20 a day, or savings that grow ₹500 a month.
In a row of hexagons made of matchsticks, the first needs 6 and each new one needs 5 more, so n hexagons need 5n + 1 sticks. Area also grows linearly when only one side grows in equal steps.

example.q: Tiles: stage 1 has 4, stage 2 has 7, stage 3 has 10. Find the rule and the stage with 61 tiles.

learn.reallife: Stacked chairs in a school hall: each extra chair adds the same height, so the stack height follows a linear rule.

quiz.q: A tile pattern has 2n − 1 tiles at stage n. How many tiles are at stage 25?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract 1

quiz.q: A row of n hexagons needs 5n + 1 matchsticks. How many sticks for 12 hexagons?
quiz.mistake: Uses 6 sticks per hexagon, forgetting shared sides

quiz.q: Can exactly 100 matchsticks make a complete row of hexagons using the rule 5n + 1?
options: No, n would be 19.8, not a whole number
quiz.mistake: Rounds the stage number and says yes

quiz.q: An auto-rickshaw charges ₹25 plus ₹14 per km. What is the fare for 9 km?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the fixed charge by the distance too

quiz.q: Ishaan has ₹360 pocket money and spends ₹24 each day. After how many days will it run out?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the wrong number

quiz.q: A pattern goes 7, 11, 15, 19, ... Which stage has 87 in it?
quiz.mistake: Divides 87 by 4 without using the rule

quiz.q: A rectangle is 5 cm wide. Its length is 2 cm, 3 cm, 4 cm, ... growing 1 cm each step. By how much does its area grow each step?
quiz.explain: Each extra 1 cm of length adds a 5 cm × 1 cm strip.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the area grows by the same 1 cm as the length

quiz.q: Divya saves ₹800 at the start and adds ₹350 each month. How much does she have after 10 months?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the starting amount

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Tiles go 1, 3, 5, 7. How do I find stage 100 without drawing?"
teach.praise: Hooray! Same jump each time gives a rule like 2n − 1 for any stage!
teach.nudge: What stays the same from one stage to the next? Can you write a rule with n?

learn.hook: A plant grows 2 cm a week, a phone loses ₹1500 of value a year: both change by the same amount each step!
points: Linear growth: a quantity increases by a fixed amount in each equal time interval.
Linear decay: a quantity decreases by a fixed amount in each equal time interval.
Make a table of values, spot the fixed change, and write the rule as start + change × time, e.g. cost C(d) = 100 + 60d.
For decay the change is negative: a tank with 3 m of water draining 0.5 m per hour has h(t) = 3 − 0.5t.
Examples: plant height, a town gaining the same number of people every year, a phone's value dropping by a fixed amount, prepaid balance running out.

example.q: A tank holds water 3 m deep and loses 0.5 m every hour. Write h(t) and find when it is empty.

learn.reallife: A metro card that loses ₹40 per daily trip shows linear decay: you can predict the day it needs a recharge.

games.title: Growth or decay?
items: Height of a sapling +3 cm per week

items.text: Start 3 m, −0.5 m per hour: h(t) = ___.
Plant 10 cm, +2 cm per week: H(w) = ___.

quiz.q: A cycle on rent costs ₹100 plus ₹60 per day, C(d) = 100 + 60d. What is the cost for 5 days?
quiz.explain: Substitute d = 5.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the fixed ₹100

quiz.q: Using h(t) = 3 − 0.5t (metres), how deep is the water after 4 hours?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracts for decay

quiz.q: A sapling is 12 cm tall and grows 3 cm every week. How tall is it after 8 weeks?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the starting height by the weeks

quiz.q: A phone bought for ₹18,000 loses ₹2,500 in value each year. What is it worth after 4 years?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one year's loss

quiz.q: A prepaid balance of ₹450 drops by ₹30 per day. On which day does it reach zero?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 30 once instead of dividing

quiz.q: A table shows a town's population: 2020: 5000, 2021: 5150, 2022: 5300. What kind of change is this?
quiz.explain: Each year the population rises by the same 150.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any increase means doubling

quiz.q: Which rule shows linear decay?
quiz.explain: The value drops by a fixed 75 in each time step.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a large starting number means decay

quiz.q: Using V(t) = 900 − 75t, after how many years is V = 300?
quiz.mistake: Divides 300 by 75 instead of 600

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What's the difference between linear growth and linear decay?"
teach.praise: Exactly! Same amount up each step is growth, same amount down is decay!
teach.nudge: Does the amount change by the same number each step? Which way does it go in decay?

topics.title: Finding a linear rule from two points

learn.hook: Two bills from a tiffin service are enough to crack its secret pricing rule!
points: A linear relationship between x and y has the form y = ax + b.
Given two pairs (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), substitute each to get two equations; subtracting them gives a, and then b.
Meaning: a is the rate per unit (₹ per km, cm per week); b is the fixed amount when x = 0 (a fixed charge or a starting value).
Axis intercepts: the line meets the y-axis at (0, b) and the x-axis where y = 0, at x = −b/a.

example.q: A tiffin service charges ₹520 for 6 meals and ₹820 for 11 meals. Find the rule.

learn.reallife: Water bills, taxi fares and gym fees often hide a fixed charge plus a rate. Two bills reveal both.

games.title: What do a and b mean?

quiz.q: A line y = ax + b passes through (1, 5) and (3, 11). What is a?
quiz.explain: Subtract the equations: 11 − 5 = (3 − 1)a, so 6 = 2a.
quiz.mistake: Divides 11 by 3 directly

quiz.q: For the same line through (1, 5) and (3, 11), what is b?
quiz.explain: Put a = 3 into 5 = a + b.
quiz.mistake: Uses the y-value as b

quiz.q: A plumber charges ₹650 for a 3-hour job and ₹1050 for a 5-hour job. What is his hourly rate?
quiz.explain: The extra 2 hours cost 1050 − 650 = ₹400.
quiz.mistake: Divides one bill by its hours, which mixes in the fixed charge

quiz.q: For the same plumber, what is the fixed visiting charge?
quiz.mistake: Confuses the fixed charge with the rate

quiz.q: In the rule y = 12x + 35 for a gym (x months), what does 35 stand for?
options: The total fee for a year
quiz.explain: b is the value when x = 0: what you pay before any month is counted.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rate with the fixed amount

quiz.q: A line passes through (0, −4) and (2, 0). What is its rule?
quiz.explain: b = −4 from (0, −4). Then 0 = 2a − 4 gives a = 2.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the roles of the two intercepts

quiz.q: Where does the line y = 3x − 9 meet the x-axis?
quiz.mistake: Gives the y-intercept instead

quiz.q: A linear polynomial p(x) has p(2) = 1 and p(6) = 9. What is p(0)?
quiz.mistake: Assumes p(0) is 0 for every polynomial

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "If I know two bills, how do I find the rate and the fixed charge?"
teach.praise: Smart! Two equations, subtract to get the rate, then find the fixed part!
teach.nudge: How many equations do the two bills give you? What does b tell you?

learn.hook: Water freezes at 0 °C and at 32 °F. Two fixed points are all you need to link the scales!
points: Celsius and Fahrenheit are linearly related. Using freezing (0 °C, 32 °F) and boiling (100 °C, 212 °F): F = (9/5)C + 32.
So 100 Celsius degrees cover 180 Fahrenheit degrees: each 1 °C step is 1.8 °F.
Kelvin starts at absolute zero: K = C + 273.15, so F = (9/5)(K − 273.15) + 32.
Work done by a constant force: W = F × d (joules = newtons × metres). For a fixed force, W is a linear function of d whose graph is a straight line through the origin.
learn.reallife: Weather apps switch between °C and °F using exactly this linear rule, and a fever of 100.4 °F is 38 °C.

quiz.q: Convert 25 °C to Fahrenheit (in °F).
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add 32

quiz.q: A thermometer shows 104 °F. What is this in Celsius (°C)?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 32 but forgets to multiply by 5/9

quiz.q: Using freezing (0, 32) and boiling (100, 212) as (C, F) points, what is the slope of F against C?
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way, getting 5/9

quiz.q: At which temperature are the Celsius and Fahrenheit readings equal?
quiz.explain: Set F = C: C = 1.8C + 32 gives −0.8C = 32, so C = −40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the scales agree at 0

quiz.q: Convert 310.15 K to Fahrenheit (°F).
quiz.mistake: Stops at the Celsius value

quiz.q: Convert 50 °F to kelvin (K).
quiz.mistake: Adds 273.15 to the Fahrenheit value

quiz.q: A coolie pushes a trolley with a steady force of 40 N for 25 m. How much work is done (in joules)?
quiz.mistake: Adds force and distance

quiz.q: For a fixed force of 30 N, what does the graph of work W against distance d look like?
options: A straight line cutting the W-axis at 30
A straight line through the origin with slope 30
quiz.explain: W = 30d is linear with b = 0, so it passes through (0, 0) and rises 30 J per metre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the force value is the intercept

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I change Celsius into Fahrenheit?"
teach.nudge: What do you multiply the Celsius value by? What do you add afterwards?

learn.hook: Put a linear polynomial on a graph and something magical happens: every point falls in one perfectly straight line!
points: To graph y = ax + b, make a table: choose some x-values, work out y, plot the points (x, y) and join them.
The graph of a linear polynomial is always a straight line. Two points are enough to draw it; a third point is a good check.
b is where the line cuts the y-axis: the point (0, b).
a is the slope: when x increases by 1, y changes by a. If a > 0 the line rises; if a < 0 it falls.
Lines with the same a (same slope) are parallel.

example.q: Draw the graph of y = 2x + 1 using x = 0, 1, 2.
steps: Plot and join: a rising straight line cutting the y-axis at (0, 1); y goes up by 2 for each step of 1 in x

learn.reallife: A plot of distance against time for a train moving at steady speed is a straight line; the steeper the line, the faster the train.

games.title: Which point is on which line?
Line talk
items: The graph of y = 5x − 1 is a straight line
Every linear polynomial has a straight-line graph.
The line y = −3x + 2 rises from left to right
The slope −3 is negative, so the line falls as x increases.
The line y = 4x + 7 cuts the y-axis at (0, 7)
You need at least five points to draw the graph of a linear polynomial
Two points fix a straight line; a third is only a check.
The lines y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 are parallel
Both have slope 2, so they rise at the same rate and never meet.

quiz.q: What does the graph of y = 4x − 3 look like?
quiz.explain: y = 4x − 3 is a linear polynomial, and every linear polynomial has a straight-line graph.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative constant bends the graph

quiz.q: Where does the line y = 3x + 5 cut the y-axis?
quiz.explain: On the y-axis x = 0, so y = 3 × 0 + 5 = 5. The point is (0, 5).
quiz.mistake: Writes the intercept as (5, 0), swapping x and y

quiz.q: For y = 2x − 1, what is y when x = 4?
quiz.explain: Substitute x = 4: 2 × 4 − 1 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Which line falls as x increases?
quiz.explain: A line falls when its slope (the coefficient of x) is negative. Only y = −3x + 1 has a negative slope.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the sign of the constant term instead of the coefficient of x

quiz.q: On the graph of y = 5x + 2, by how much does y increase when x goes up by 1?
quiz.explain: The coefficient of x is the slope. Each step of 1 in x adds 5 to y.
quiz.mistake: Chooses the constant term instead of the slope

quiz.q: Which point lies on the line y = −2x + 6?
quiz.explain: Check each point: for x = 1, y = −2 + 6 = 4, so (1, 4) is on the line.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus sign on the slope

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹100 and saves ₹20 every week, so his savings after x weeks are y = 20x + 100. After how many weeks will he have ₹260?
quiz.mistake: Divides 260 by 20 without removing the starting ₹100

quiz.q: A line passes through (0, 1) and (2, 7). Which equation does it show?
quiz.explain: It cuts the y-axis at 1, so b = 1. From x = 0 to x = 2, y rises by 6, so the slope is 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses the total rise 6 as the slope without dividing by the run 2

teach.ask: Gappu has graph paper and a ruler: "How do I draw y = 2x + 1? Do I have to plot hundreds of points?"
teach.praise: Make a small table, plot two or three points and join them with a ruler. A perfect straight line!
teach.nudge: How many points do I really need, and what shape will I get?

topics.title: Slope: how steep and which way

learn.hook: Two roads climb a hill. One rises 1 m in every 10 m, the other 1 m in every 4 m. Slope tells you which one makes your cycle legs ache!
points: Slope from two points: a = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁), rise over run.
When b = 0 the line y = ax passes through the origin (0, 0).
A positive slope rises from left to right (growth); a negative slope falls (decay); slope 0 is a horizontal line.
The bigger |a| is, the steeper the line: y = 5x is steeper than y = 2x, and y = −4x is steeper than y = −x.

example.q: Find the slope of the line through (−1, 7) and (3, −1). Does it rise or fall?

learn.reallife: Railway engineers keep tracks at gentle slopes; a ghat road sign showing a steep gradient warns trucks to use low gear.

quiz.q: What is the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
quiz.mistake: Divides run by rise

quiz.q: What is the slope of the line through (−2, 5) and (4, −7)?
quiz.mistake: Loses the minus sign

quiz.q: Which of these lines goes through the point (0, 0)?
quiz.explain: Only y = −7x has b = 0, so x = 0 gives y = 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any line with a negative slope passes through the origin

quiz.q: Which line is the steepest?
quiz.explain: Steepness depends on |a|. |−5| = 5 is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Ignores negative slopes when comparing steepness

quiz.q: A line through the origin passes through (4, 10). What is its slope?
quiz.explain: For y = ax through (0, 0), a = 10 ÷ 4.
quiz.mistake: Divides x by y

quiz.q: A graph of a candle's length against time falls from left to right. What does this tell you about a?
options: a is positive: the length grows
a is negative: the length decreases
quiz.explain: A falling line has negative slope, matching decay.
quiz.mistake: Links a falling line with a positive slope

quiz.q: The slope of the line through (1, 4) and (5, 4) is:
quiz.explain: Rise = 0, so slope = 0 ÷ 4 = 0. The line is horizontal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a horizontal line has no slope at all

quiz.q: Riya's savings graph rises ₹150 per week and Amit's rises ₹90 per week. Whose line is steeper?
quiz.explain: A larger rate (slope) gives a steeper line; 150 > 90.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the line that starts higher is steeper

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the slope from two points, and what does a negative slope look like?"
teach.praise: Brilliant! Rise over run, and negative means the line goes down!
teach.nudge: What do you divide by what to get the slope? Which way does a negative slope go?

learn.hook: Change one number in y = ax + b and watch a whole family of lines spin or slide!
points: Lines with the same slope a are parallel: y = 2x, y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x − 4 never meet.
Changing b with a fixed slides the line up (b bigger) or down (b smaller) without turning it.
Changing a with b fixed turns the line about the point (0, b): all of y = ax + 3 pass through (0, 3).
In the family f(x) = ax + a = a(x + 1), every line passes through (−1, 0), because f(−1) = 0 for any a. The slope and the y-intercept are both a.

example.q: Show that y = 4x + 4 and y = −2x − 2 both pass through (−1, 0).
steps: Both are of the form ax + a

learn.reallife: A graph of several mobile plans with the same per-GB rate but different fixed fees shows parallel lines: the cheapest is the lowest one.

games.title: Family facts
items: All lines y = ax + 6 pass through (0, 6).
At x = 0, y = 6 whatever a is.
Every line of the form y = ax + a passes through (1, 0).
Increasing b moves the line y = ax + b upward.
Every y-value goes up by the same amount.

quiz.q: Which line is parallel to y = −3x + 7?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines have equal slopes; −3 matches.
quiz.mistake: Matches the intercept instead of the slope

quiz.q: The line y = 2x + 1 is moved up by 4 units. What is the new equation?
quiz.explain: Shifting up adds 4 to b; the slope stays 2.
quiz.mistake: Changes the slope instead of the intercept

quiz.q: Lines y = ax + 3 for different values of a all share which point?
quiz.explain: Put x = 0: y = 3 for every a.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the x- and y-intercepts

quiz.q: Which point lies on every line of the form f(x) = ax + a?
quiz.explain: f(−1) = −a + a = 0 for any a.
quiz.mistake: Tries x = 1 instead of x = −1

quiz.q: For f(x) = ax + a, the y-intercept equals:
quiz.mistake: Thinks every member has the same y-intercept

quiz.q: A member of the family f(x) = ax + a passes through (2, 12). What is a?
quiz.mistake: Uses only the 2a part

quiz.q: Two lines y = 4x + b₁ and y = 4x + b₂ with b₁ ≠ b₂ meet at how many points?
quiz.explain: They are parallel (same slope) and distinct, so they never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every two lines must cross once

quiz.q: Ayaan draws y = x, y = 2x and y = 3x. What do the three lines have in common?
options: They all cut the y-axis at 1
They all fall from left to right
They all pass through the origin and get steeper as a grows
quiz.explain: b = 0 for each, so all pass through (0, 0); larger a means steeper.
quiz.mistake: Thinks lines through one point are parallel

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "When are two lines parallel, and what does changing b do?"
teach.praise: Superb! Same slope means parallel, and b slides the line up or down!
teach.nudge: What must be equal for lines to be parallel? What happens to a line if b gets bigger?
